title: Remote entanglement need not be the bottleneck for modular trapped-ion quantum computing
summary: Modularity underpins classical computing; as quantum processors encounter limits on fabrication yield, reliability, and size, they will also need it acutely. The bottleneck to linking modules is producing shared entanglement at sufficient rate, density, and fidelity. Trapped ions hold the best demonstrated photonic links, yet they rely on bulky collection optics that cap how densely links can be packed, and remote entanglement operations trail local gates by two orders of magnitude in rate and fidelity.
